title: Lam and imec Expand Collaboration to Advance Manufacturability of Next-Gen 3D Integration Technologies, Explore Aether Dry Resist Use Cases
summary: Lam and imec are expanding joint R&D to accelerate manufacturing readiness.

- AI computing is driving demand for advanced packaging and 3D integration.
- Lam and imec are expanding joint R&D to accelerate manufacturing readiness.
- The collaboration now includes Aether® dry resist for high-NA EUV patterning.
- The work supports future AI logic, memory, and heterogeneous integration technologies.


Training and deploying large AI models requires unprecedented computing power, memory bandwidth, and energy efficiency. Meeting those demands is no longer just about scaling transistors. Increasingly, it is about how chips are designed, connected, packaged, and manufactured as complete systems.


The industry's answer is taking shape in three dimensions.


3D integration, advanced packaging, next-generation memory architectures, and new patterning technologies are emerging as critical enablers of AI computing. Together, they allow chipmakers to break through traditional scaling constraints and deliver the performance gains required for the AI era. In this context, Lam has extended its long-standing strategic collaboration with imec, a world-leading research and innovation center in advanced semiconductor technologies, to include two new joint research and development focuses: enabling advanced 3D integration and advancing Aether® dry resist for future high-NA EUV patterning.


### AI Is Redefining How Semiconductor Performance Scales


The most advanced AI systems rely on tightly integrated combinations of logic, memory, and interconnect technologies. Moving data efficiently between these elements has become just as important as improving individual transistor performance.


That reality is driving increased adoption of advanced packaging and chiplet architectures that combine multiple specialized chips into a single system. Three-dimensional integration allows chipmakers to increase performance, memory capacity, and bandwidth while improving energy efficiency. As traditional transistor scaling becomes more challenging, advanced packaging has become a critical path for extending semiconductor performance.


But making these architectures manufacturable at scale requires innovation across materials, deposition, etch, patterning, and integration.


This is where collaborative innovation becomes essential.


### Lam and imec Advance Manufacturing Readiness for 3D Integration


Lam and imec are collaborating to accelerate manufacturing readiness for 3D integration technologies supporting advanced packaging and next-generation memory.


By bringing together Lam's deep capabilities in deposition and etch with imec’s world-class integration infrastructure, the collaboration is designed to boost the velocity with which promising innovations move from the lab to high-volume manufacturing. The collaboration focuses on key process challenges that must be solved before heterogeneous integration can scale broadly across the industry. Areas of joint research include thick dielectric deposition, asymmetric stress compensation, bevel deposition, and plasma dicing, alongside process validation for advanced packaging and future memory architectures.


The work also extends into future 3D memory technologies, including new charge-trap materials, precision multilayer deposition, high-aspect-ratio channel etch, deep memory contacts, and low-resistivity interconnects. These innovations are increasingly important as AI workloads drive demand for greater memory density and bandwidth.


### Aether Dry Resist Enables the Next Era of High-NA EUV Patterning


While advanced packaging and 3D integration help scale systems, AI also depends on continued advances in leading-edge logic devices.


As the industry approaches angstrom-era nodes, high-NA EUV lithography is required to enable smaller features and increased transistor density. However, high-NA EUV requires innovations in related technologies in resists, mask design, patterning, materials, deposition, etch, and device integration.


To address these challenges, Lam and imec are also collaborating on research and development to advance the application of Lam's Aether dry resist platform. Using imec's high-NA EUV research environment, the joint work is focused on enhancing resolution, sensitivity, depth of focus and stochastic defectivity.


The collaboration includes exploring Aether-enabled patterning for advanced interconnects, including ruthenium direct metal etch at increasingly aggressive pitches. These innovations are intended to support lower-resistivity interconnects and improved electrical performance for future logic nodes.


Importantly, the potential of Aether has already been demonstrated through joint research that achieved single-exposure high-NA EUV patterning for sub-20 nm ruthenium direct metal etch interconnects. Across the wafer that work obtained 100% electrical yield for fork structures sensitive to bridges and >90% for meander structures sensitive to breaks, at 20nm pitch. Aether-enabled patterning was highlighted as a possible path toward reduced multi-patterning complexity and improved manufacturability.


Together with Lam's Akara® etch systems and Striker® ALD portfolio, Aether is part of a broader approach to enabling the gate-all-around (GAA) and complementary FET (CFET) architectures expected to power future generations of AI computing.


### Accelerating the Pace of Semiconductor Innovation for AI


The AI era is increasing both the complexity and urgency of semiconductor innovation. Breakthroughs must happen across the entire technology stack, from advanced patterning and transistor architectures to memory, packaging, and system integration.


These new areas of collaboration research reflects Lam’s core belief that meaningful technology progress happens faster when ecosystem leaders work together to solve manufacturing challenges early and convert research breakthroughs into scalable production solutions.


Whether enabling next-generation 3D integration or advancing Aether dry resist for high-NA EUV, the objective is the same: increase the velocity at which breakthrough ideas become manufacturable technologies.


***Anand Murthy** is vice president of Advanced Technology Integration.*
